instruction: Buy me the top-rated gaming console controller that's available now on amazon for each of my siblings, and have it delivered to their homes with gift wrapping. I want to give them identical gifts.
notes: The number of siblings is only known at runtime (phone.search_contacts with relationship=sibling); the problem models two siblings as placeholders (sibling-1, sibling-2) and the per-sibling objects (address parts, address id) must be replicated per discovered sibling. The agent must buy one identical top-rated, in-stock gaming console controller per sibling, each as a separate order shipped to that sibling's home with gift wrapping. Modeled as a loop per sibling: add_address (fields parsed from the contact's home_address), add_product_to_cart with quantity 1 and clear_cart_first=true (so pre-existing cart items never pollute the order), add_gift_wrapping_to_product with quantity 1, then place_order with the amazon payment card and the new address; place_order empties the cart in the model so the loop repeats for the next sibling. search_products uses product_type and sort_by=-rating (if sorting is unsupported, pick the max-rating in-stock product from the results). supervisor.complete_task requires two distinct siblings to have the same product gift-ordered (equality constraint stands in for a universal condition) and is the last step; no answer is passed.

plan: (amazon-add-address name-sibling-1 street-sibling-1 city-sibling-1 state-sibling-1 country-sibling-1 zip-sibling-1 amazon-token sibling-1 home-address-sibling-1)
(amazon-add-address name-sibling-2 street-sibling-2 city-sibling-2 state-sibling-2 country-sibling-2 zip-sibling-2 amazon-token sibling-2 home-address-sibling-2)
